text:
jess: Noticed sustained tx_drops + retransmits on rack-r3-gpu12 during a batch preprocessing job at ~13:45 UTC. Looks like many small TLS uploads to artifacts + heavy KV cache churn from a model warmup. Logs: 

```
[13:44:58] host=rack-r3-gpu12 iface=eth0 tx_drops=37 qlen=300
[13:45:01] kvcache_evictions=120 evict_rate=25/s allocs=[alloc-c12, alloc-d44] tenants=[tenant-mlbatch, tenant-stream]
[13:45:10] retransmits=64 timeouts=3
```

priya: ugh. Is this the same pattern as last week's small-packet artifact storm? Any differences?

samir: Similar surface, but this one has a big spike in kvcache_evictions. The tokenizer pipeline is doing many parallel range reads then uploading aux artifacts. qdisc gets overloaded, we start dropping tx. Not RDMA.

li: Could we try coalescing artifact uploads on the client side (few larger PUTs) as a short-term mitigation? Pushing a library bump might help but will take time.

aaron: For immediate relief: 1) throttle per-tenant egress with token-bucket on fractional slices, 2) add a temporary soft-route that sends tenant-mlbatch to dedicated-warm pool with prewarmed KV image. That will cost ~15% extra (reserved GPUs + egress) but reduces tail.

jess: Agreed. Also we discussed NIC-aware placement on the scheduler; add two tags: "egress_hot" and "kv_thrash" so we avoid colocating with egress-heavy cache-warmups. Priya can we scope the scheduler change?

priya: I can spec it. Need input on signal sources: should kvcache_evictions > 50/min plus tx_drops > 10 trigger egress_hot? Also need to surface tenant labels for billing.

samir: Those thresholds seem reasonable for a start. Also consider qdisc tuning (fq_codel or ingress shaping) on the GPU host class. That's a low-risk kernel tweak.

ops-bot: ALERT: egress_tx_errors=98 on rack-r3-gpu12 (window=10m). Linked allocs: alloc-c12, alloc-d44.

li: For rollout plan: canary the fq_codel changes on 10 hosts in eu-west with a weekend low-traffic window. If stable, expand. I'll open a ticket and coordinate with oncall.

jess: Please file TICKET-8342 for the canary + scheduler tag design. Also create a short runbook: prefer soft-route to dedicated-warm pool (avoid mass evacuation).

ops-bot: Scheduled cfg-1105: deploy /etc/sysctl.d/fq_codel_gpu.conf to 10 hosts starting in 6h UTC in batches of 2.

aaron: Cost note: routing to dedicated-warm adds reserved GPU spend + outbound egress on different network tier. Estimate ~15% uplift for the rerouted workload. Recommend we have an opt-in billing flag for enterprise tenants to accept this during incidents.

priya: I'll add the billing flag and the scheduler patch to the spec. Can we also add a probe that detects prewarmable models (image fingerprint) so we can avoid unnecessary warmups?

samir: Good idea. Probe + client-coalesce + fq_codel + soft-route should reduce recurrence. We'll also add a metric dashboard for kvcache_evictions vs tx_drops.

jess: Thanks. Keep updates here. If the canary shows any unexpected cross-host hotfilling, pause and revert the soft-route. :thumbsup:

li: Opening TICKET-8342 now and assigning to infra-team. Will post PR links when ready.
